outcomes.text: Recognise what a text, recording or data display says outright
Pick out the supporting or relevant details in a source
Find data points, patterns and trends in charts and graphs
Work out meaning beyond the surface of a source
Identify the main idea, theme or purpose
Work out who a source is meant for
Identify point of view, tone or attitude
Spot the organising and rhetorical structures or strategies used
Work out unknown words and phrases from textual cues
Combine and infer meaning across sources
Link information within or between sources
Combine ideas from sources to reach logical conclusions
Infer unstated meaning from context

units.title: Skill Category 2: Interpersonal and Presentational Communication

topics.title: 2.A Use language that fits purpose and context

outcomes.text: Use language suited to the purpose and setting of the communication
Use a range of grammatical structures
Use a range of vocabulary
Use idiomatic, culturally appropriate expressions
Choose a register suited to audience and situation
Make speech and writing easy for the intended audience to understand
Use circumlocution and paraphrase to get around gaps
Monitor own speech, spot mistakes and self-correct
Pronounce clearly enough for varied speakers to understand
Use suitable speed and intonation when speaking
Follow written conventions: capitals, spelling, accents, punctuation
Share ideas, information and opinions on familiar and researched topics
Express ideas, preferences and opinions
Use research strategies to gather information and evidence
Give examples to advise, inform and explain opinions or feelings
Combine several sources to build and support a position
Refer to and cite sources properly
Organise and connect ideas with suitable strategies
Use an appropriate organisational structure
Use cohesive devices such as relative pronouns, referents, conjunctions and transitions
